decisions.reason: As a flagship digital anamnesis and consent app, it is tightly linked to the firm's existing dental workflow, compliance, and integration knowledge, giving it strong scope for continued learning and improvement.

A continuing education institute uses some of the firm's training and customer access capabilities, but it is more distant from its core software development and product-integration knowledge, so absorptive capacity for improving it commercially is weaker.
A remote screen sharing support tool fits the firm's established support, implementation, and customer service routines and directly complements its installed software base.
A practice performance analytics dashboard builds directly on the firm's data, workflow, and practice-management expertise, making it highly learnable and improvable from customer usage.

A complete dental practice bundle is essentially a commercialization of the firm's existing modular software and integration capabilities, so it sits very close to the knowledge base of the core business.

A job and practice listing portal is the least related to the firm's core practice-software competencies and depends more on marketplace dynamics than on knowledge the firm already strongly possesses.
